drake-pmo is kept private by the operator’s 2026-11-15 decision: it stays private until a project other than drake-pmo actually uses a work order. The trigger is measurable as any non-`drake-pmo` `product_id` in `pmo/work-orders` whose emitter output was merged; one product is enough. The context also notes that public visibility would publish an assessment of five other people’s repositories’ engineering choices.
The “Know Your Cash” diagnostic costs $1,500 fixed-price. It has a 7-day turnaround and is credited in full against the first two months of the $1,200/mo retainer if the client signs within 14 days.

The buyer for the outbound consulting offer is the bookkeeper / fractional CFO who already owns 5–15 landscaping clients, not the end owner. The offer is sold as the artifact and the day to the bookkeeper, and SKU 1 reaches buyers through the partner rather than cold outreach to the owner. No other buyer is named for that offer in the context.

Under the ACTIVE gate policy dated 2026-10-01, approved by the operator for the R1 proposal, an un-authored CHECK is treated as a baseline gap rather than a work failure. This applies when a criterion has no CHECK authored, meaning the baseline is incomplete because nobody wrote a command so it can never run. The new treatment is `unrunnable`, which allows a PR but leaves the slice not fully proven.

The slice dependency tree validator fails on dependency cycles, dependencies missing from the tree, gate/state mismatches, and invalid states. It also errors when a tree edit touches a slice that is `state=ready` AND `automation_eligible=true` outside the orchestrator’s own transitions.
